newsitem.title: USA: House lawmakers urge mayors to oppose new air rule.
newsitem.headline: House lawmakers urge mayors to oppose new air rule.

text.p: Two House Democrats urged mayors meeting in San Francisco this week to back a resolution opposing a plan by the Environmental Protection Agency to set strict new limits on smog and soot.

In a June 20 letter released Monday, Reps. John Dingell and Ron Klink, who represent districts in Detroit and Pittsburgh, asked Chicago Mayor Richard Daley, president of the U.S. Conference of Mayors, to support the resolution by the mayors of Dearborn and Detroit, Michigan.

Mayors were expected to vote Tuesday on the resolution, which calls for the EPA to stick with current standards for smog-forming ozone and fine particles rather than tightening them as it proposed last November.

If the plan, which the agency is expected to finalise in the next few days, goes through, hundreds of counties that now meet air quality standards will be thrown out of compliance, Dingell and Klink wrote. If an area does not meet new standards it could eventually be subject to "strict, automatic sanctions, including the loss of highway funds," they said.

"While the EPA may claim that they will -- through nimble statutory readings and other artifices -- minimise the impact of these provisions, EPA cannot guarantee that third parties will not force EPA to enforce the letter of the law including the sanctions provisions," the letter said.
Republicans have urged the Clinton administration not to go ahead with the proposed rules until more research is done on the health impact of fine particles.

Democrats are divided over whether to support stricter clean air standards, with lawmakers from cities that depend on steel, car, and fossil fuel industries opposing the new rules and lawmakers from the Northeast seeking stricter standards on upwind areas that blow pollution into their region.
